_about: Changes since the last deploy go in "unreleased", each tagged kind fix/feature/breaking. On deploy, tools/release-notes/release.py turns them into the next release (newest first) and sets the version. See CLAUDE.md, Versioning.

fixes.title: AI gateway with a fallback notice
fixes.text: Model calls can now go through a shared AI gateway that picks the provider. If the gateway is down, calls carry on using the free providers, and a dismissible banner at the top of the page says so.

fixes.title: Cloudflare model back to Qwen 3.8
fixes.text: Cloudflare retired the faster **qwen3-30b-a3b** model, so every call to it failed. Agents on Cloudflare now use **qwen3.8-27b** again, a saved choice of the old model is switched over, and short calls such as **Where to next** answer without spending their allowance thinking.

fixes.title: Image and document jobs research with a team
fixes.text: A job whose Focus is an image or documents now works like a keyword job: the agent splits the research across 2 or more workers, each shown with its own card, searches the web beyond what the material shows, and writes a report from what they find, instead of answering from the material and general knowledge alone.

fixes.title: Focus on keywords, an image or documents
fixes.text: The Focus step has **Keywords**, **Image** and **Document** tabs, and the chosen tab alone is the job. An image is read once by a vision model and the agent works from that reading; up to three PDF, Word, text or CSV documents are read and analysed on every turn, quoted and compared by name.

fixes.title: Task topics work on the subject
fixes.text: A Focus topic that is something to do or make, like **Create Images**, is now applied to the other topics instead of treated as a subject of its own. **Augustus** with **Create Images** researches Augustus and makes images of him, in the way the Character works, rather than looking up a company called Create Images.

fixes.title: Open a saved file from the reply
fixes.text: When an agent saves a file and names it in its reply, the file name is now a button that opens the file, instead of a path on the server.

fixes.title: Files you ask for are built for you
fixes.text: Asking an agent to save, export or download something (a template, document, spreadsheet) now builds a real file in the best format straight away, ready to preview and download. Agents no longer write their own save tool, which could report a file as saved when it was empty.

fixes.title: Location per job
fixes.text: The location now sits under Type on the Character step. Each job starts with your location from Settings, can be given its own on the map, and keeps it when saved. A round tickbox beside it decides whether the agent uses it at all.

fixes.title: Model and Settings at the end of the header
fixes.text: The model and web search lines sit in a column at the right end of the agent header, in smaller plain text, with a Settings button beside them the same size as the toolbar buttons. The deployment page now has Settings too: a model, location or search change there applies from the agent's next reply.

fixes.title: Brief choices you can click
fixes.text: When the brief spots a tension or gap in your Focus, it says how the agent will handle it and offers buttons to change course: **Lead with** a topic (the agent then frames the job around it), **Drop** one, or **Add** one. The brief no longer asks you to clarify things you can't type.

fixes.title: Where to next is back on Cloudflare
fixes.text: On Cloudflare's Qwen, short calls such as suggesting where to go next spent their whole allowance thinking and came back empty, so some replies ended without **Where to next**. Those calls now answer straight away. The box under the latest reply, now labelled **Answer or direct the Agent**, also shows even when there are no routes.

fixes.title: Image Focus shown on the job
fixes.text: A job whose Focus is an image shows the image's file name where the keywords go on a keyword job.

fixes.title: Tidier brief spacing
fixes.text: The written brief starts at the top of its box, with a single blank line between the text and each subheading instead of large gaps.

fixes.title: Image and document jobs start on their own
fixes.text: An agent whose Focus is an image or documents now starts work on the material as soon as the mission briefing is dismissed, as keyword jobs always did, instead of waiting for you to ask it something.

fixes.title: Focus tabs look like tabs
fixes.text: The Focus step's **Keywords**, **Image** and **Document** choices are now drawn as tabs on a rule, with the chosen one outlined and open onto its content below, both a shade lighter than the step's background, instead of pills.

fixes.title: Agent design works on Cloudflare again
fixes.text: Designing an agent on Cloudflare's Qwen could fail with **Bootstrap failed: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str**, because the model's reply sometimes ends with stray non-text pieces. Those are now skipped.

fixes.title: Deploy toolbar moved
fixes.text: The Deploy toolbar now sits under the flowchart in the **Build your agent** box, at its right.

fixes.title: Clearer location tickbox
fixes.text: The job's location pill is no longer faded when location isn't factored in. When it is ticked, the pill is tinted with a dark-blue border, like a selected Character pill.

fixes.title: Image jobs no longer overflow the model
fixes.text: After an agent made an image, the next step sent the whole image to the model as text, which overflowed Cloudflare's Qwen and pushed the job onto slow local Ollama. The model now sees a short reference instead, and the image is put back into the reply.

fixes.title: Full browser storage no longer breaks a job
fixes.text: When the browser's storage was full, saving a job crashed the job screen. Now a job that doesn't fit is saved without its generated images, and if it still doesn't fit it isn't saved; your other saved jobs are never removed to make room.

fixes.title: Quieter brief progress
fixes.text: The brief's progress line (such as **Writing the brief in one go**) is a little smaller, in the same uppercase lettering as the section labels, with a smaller spinner.

fixes.title: Graphs follow the newest step
fixes.text: When a step is added or updated in the brief graph, it scrolls to the right so the newest step is in view. Setup's process graph stays where it is, since its steps are how you move between pages.

fixes.title: Character pills match the Focus topics
fixes.text: The Type, Personality and Behaviour pills on the Character step now look like the Focus topics: unselected ones white, selected ones tinted with a dark-blue border, all with the same rounded corners.

fixes.title: Sub-headings in replies are dark blue
fixes.text: Third-level headings in an agent's reply (e.g. "Key Features of This Template") were near-black; they now use the same dark blue as the other headings.

fixes.title: A briefer brief
fixes.text: The written brief in Setup is now three short groups of dot points instead of three paragraphs, each under a heading written for that agent: what the topics add up to, how its character shapes the work, and what it will do. The bullets are larger than the text.

fixes.title: AI methods document in Settings
fixes.text: Settings has a new **AI methods document** section: download a PDF of the AI features, approaches and methods used across the projects, with how each is used and what it does. When running locally it can also regenerate the PDF from each project's own docs.

fixes.title: Edit a Focus topic in place
fixes.text: Click a selected Focus topic to edit its text; Enter or clicking away saves, Escape cancels. Saved Focus topics are unchanged.

fixes.title: Resume continues the last job
fixes.text: In **Load Agent**, a built profile's **Launch** button is now **Resume**. It opens the built agent and continues its last saved job, with no rebuild. **Recommission** on the deployment screen starts it fresh.

fixes.title: Resume a saved job
fixes.text: In **Load Agent**, a saved job now has a **Resume** button that continues that chat where it left off, with all its messages.

fixes.title: Chats save themselves
fixes.text: Every chat is now saved after each reply, so reloading the page or opening a new tab picks it up where you left off. **Settings → On reload or new tab** can switch this to start again at Setup instead.

fixes.title: Settings button in the header
fixes.text: On Setup, the **Settings** button now sits in the header to the right of the model and web search, slightly larger.

fixes.title: Keep or clear when going back to Setup
fixes.text: Going back to Setup from the deployment screen now asks whether to **Keep** the agent's Focus topics and character in the steps, or **Clear** them all and start again.

fixes.title: Tidier Settings
fixes.text: Each setting in Settings now sits in its own box with its heading, with even spacing throughout.

fixes.title: New agent starts with no Focus topics
fixes.text: **New agent** on the deployment screen now goes back to Setup with the Focus topics cleared, so no brief starts drafting until you choose new ones. **Recommission** still restarts the same agent.

fixes.title: Uppercase Focus topics on the deployment screen
fixes.text: The Focus topics shown under the deployment screen's top toolbar are now always in uppercase, in the same lighter steel blue as Focus topics in Setup.

fixes.title: Or ask a question
fixes.text: Under the latest answer's Where to next options there is now a box to ask the agent your own question directly.

fixes.title: Brief questions stand out
fixes.text: When the brief needs to ask you something, Setup opens the Brief step, and the Brief box in the build graph turns the same colour as the question.

fixes.title: Model on the right in the deployment header
fixes.text: On the deployment page the model and web search line now sit at the far right of the header, as they do on Setup.

fixes.title: Case file before Where to next
fixes.text: Under each answer, the case file and export bar now comes before the Where to next options, with a clear gap between them.

fixes.title: Case file before the reply's Next steps
fixes.text: When a reply ends with its own **Next steps** list, the Case file and export bar now sits above that list, so all the follow-up choices are together at the bottom.

fixes.title: One name for the agent
fixes.text: "How this agent was made" now gives the agent the same name as the header, instead of a second name the model made up. Agents built before this keep their old name there until they are rebuilt.

fixes.title: Agents always show their web search
fixes.text: If a General or Research agent's design comes back with no way to look things up, web search is now added when it's built, so it shows in the tool row and in "How this agent was made". The agent could already search while running; it just didn't show.

releases.title: What we fixed, and the AI behind it
releases.subtitle: Agent One · 187 commits, 20 September to 17 November 2026
releases.intro: Agent One builds an agent from a plain-language goal. A model writes the agent's system prompt, picks or writes its tools, and the agent then runs a tool loop with a team of worker agents. Most of the hard problems were not in the idea but in making it **fast, cheap and dependable**: models that wrote broken tool code, a cloud model that was too slow to use, free quotas that ran out mid-session, and services that hung or silently failed. This page lists the main fixes, then the AI services the app uses and why each one is there.

headline.title: The biggest single change: the model
headline.text: Up to 17 November the default model was Cloudflare's **Qwen 3.8 27B**. It gave good answers but spent about 1,000 hidden reasoning tokens on every call, even at low reasoning effort. Switching the default to **Qwen3 30B-A3B** (a mixture-of-experts model that only uses about 3B parameters per token) is the main reason the app now feels so much faster.

releases.fixesNote: Grouped by the kind of problem. Older fixes first within each group.

groups.title: A. Speed, cost and keeping a model available

fixes.title: Paid API costs on day one
fixes.problem: Early development ran against paid cloud models, so every test cost money.
fixes.fix: Switched development to a local model (Ollama on the desktop GPU) and kept cloud models optional.
fixes.result: Unlimited free testing; the local model is still the last fallback today.

fixes.title: Gemini credits ran out
fixes.problem: Gemini's prepaid credits were used up and every call returned 402.
fixes.fix: A 402 now makes the app skip Gemini for 15 minutes instead of failing every request. Gemini became optional and Cloudflare Workers AI the main provider.
fixes.result: Requests go straight to a provider that works.

fixes.title: Cloudflare free quota lasted a few hours
fixes.problem: Workers AI's free 10,000 neurons a day ran out within hours of real use (error 4006), and the error detection missed it because the code was not reading the response body.
fixes.fix: Fixed the 4006 detection; on that error the app skips Workers AI until 00:00 UTC. Then moved the account to Workers Paid, so usage past the free allowance is billed, not refused.
fixes.result: No more mid-session outages from the daily limit.

fixes.title: One failing provider failed the whole request
fixes.problem: If the chosen model failed, the user saw an error even when another provider was up.
fixes.fix: A fallback cascade in `llm_client.py`: Gemini, then Workers AI, then local Ollama. An agent set to a free provider never falls back to paid Gemini.
fixes.result: A request succeeds as long as any allowed provider is reachable.

fixes.title: The live site failed when local worked
fixes.problem: Production returned errors while local dev was fine: the droplet's `.env` never had the Cloudflare keys, only the local `env.json` did.
fixes.fix: Added the keys on the droplet; the deploy script now treats them as required.
fixes.result: Production and local run the same providers.

fixes.title: Too slow to use
fixes.problem: Qwen 3.8 27B took 26-52 s a call; a brief took about 3 minutes.
fixes.fix: Measured both hosted models and made Qwen3 30B-A3B the default everywhere, including a one-time move for browsers that had the old default saved.
fixes.result: 3-5 s a call, 16 s a brief (see the table above).

fixes.title: Workers ran one after another
fixes.problem: A turn with several worker agents ran them in sequence, so three workers took three times as long.
fixes.fix: Workers now run in parallel threads and each result streams back as soon as it finishes. Each tool call got a `call_index` so results attach to the right card. On the single local GPU workers still run one at a time, since Ollama would only queue them.
fixes.result: A team costs about as long as its slowest worker.

fixes.title: Tool servers that hung or kept failing
fixes.problem: An MCP tool server that did not answer could hang a request, and a broken one was retried on every bootstrap.
fixes.fix: Calls have a hard timeout, and a failed server is cached as down for 5 minutes.
fixes.result: A bad tool server costs a few seconds once, not every time.

groups.title: B. Making generated agents actually work

fixes.title: The agent did not perform requests
fixes.problem: Early on the agent loop described tool calls instead of making them, so nothing was fetched.
fixes.fix: Fixed the streaming loop so tool calls are executed and their results fed back to the model.
fixes.result: The foundation for everything else.

fixes.title: Generated tools calling functions that do not exist
fixes.problem: The model wrote tool code that called `tavily_search()`, `tools.search_image()`, invented helpers like `tas_search()`, or a made-up localhost proxy. It compiled, then crashed the first time the tool ran.
fixes.fix: Three code checks run after every bootstrap: a forbidden-name scan (built-in and MCP tool names), a local-endpoint scan, and an AST check that flags any call to a name the sandbox does not provide. A failing tool gets one retry with the error, then is dropped.
fixes.result: Broken tools are caught at build time, not in front of the user.

fixes.title: Bootstrap JSON that would not parse
fixes.problem: Bootstrap often failed with “Expecting ',' delimiter”. The cause was the prompt itself: its example showed a double-quoted Python dict, which the model copied into a JSON string.
fixes.fix: Fixed the example and added a rule to single-quote strings inside tool code. The one retry now gets a hint specific to this error. A blind repair was tried and rejected as unsafe.
fixes.result: The prompt no longer teaches the model to break its own output.

fixes.title: No team, or a team the model ignored
fixes.problem: Asked about several topics, the main agent did everything itself, so no workers were used.
fixes.fix: The delegation rule went from optional to a must, with code that sends the reply back once if a research turn used fewer than two workers or skipped the report.
fixes.result: Research turns reliably use a team and a written synthesis.

fixes.title: Turns that only posted a plan
fixes.problem: A turn sometimes drew its plan diagram and stopped without doing the work.
fixes.fix: Such a turn is sent back once to carry the plan out, and the prompt says so.
fixes.result: Plans are followed through in the same turn.

fixes.title: Answers drifting out of scope
fixes.problem: Out-of-scope rules in the prompt can be paraphrased away or argued around.
fixes.fix: A separate judge model screens each final reply against the out-of-scope list; one regenerate, then a fixed, code-written decline.
fixes.result: A guarded agent cannot be talked into a forbidden topic as easily.

fixes.title: No way to search the web
fixes.problem: Agents could only fetch a known URL or search job listings.
fixes.fix: Added Tavily's official remote MCP server as a vetted tool, and gave the Setup brief a quick search so a bare name like “augustus” can be placed instead of asked about.
fixes.result: Agents and the brief work from current information.

fixes.title: Tavily's monthly credits ran out
fixes.problem: When Tavily hit its usage limit, every search failed for the rest of the month.
fixes.fix: A server that reports a usage limit is paused for an hour (a rate limit for 60 s) and left out of the tool list. Exa's free remote MCP server was added as the fallback (no key or card needed), and a search that hits a limit mid-turn is re-run on the next provider. Brief searches are cached for 24 h. Setup and Chat show which search is in use.
fixes.result: Search keeps working, at no extra cost.

fixes.title: 29-second request limit
fixes.problem: The first deployment design (AWS Lambda behind API Gateway) cut every request off at 29 s, shorter than a real agent run.
fixes.fix: Deployed as a Flask app under gunicorn and nginx on a droplet instead, with a 300 s timeout and streaming turned on end to end.
fixes.result: Long agent runs finish and stream their progress live.

fixes.title: Stores that broke with more than one process
fixes.problem: Server-side data lived in JSON files that two processes (the web app and the MCP server) could overwrite at the same time.
fixes.fix: Moved every store to one SQLite database in WAL mode with locked write transactions; old JSON files are imported once.
fixes.result: Safe concurrent writes, including rate-limit counters.

fixes.title: Generated code running inside the server
fixes.problem: Tool code written by the model ran with `exec()` in the server process, next to the API keys.
fixes.fix: Each call now runs in a fresh child process with no secrets in its environment, a 30 s kill, CPU and memory limits, no network unless the code uses it, and an import allowlist.
fixes.result: A misbehaving tool cannot read the keys or hang the server.

fixes.title: A tiny droplet under memory pressure
fixes.problem: The 1 GB droplet was swapping.
fixes.fix: One gunicorn worker with 16 threads instead of several worker processes.
fixes.result: Up to 16 agents at once in about 90 MB.

fixes.title: Old dev servers answering instead of new code
fixes.problem: A change seemed not to work because three local backends were listening on the same port and an old one kept answering.
fixes.fix: Stopped the stale processes; worth checking first whenever a fix appears to do nothing.

groups.title: E. Seeing what the agent does

fixes.title: Long silences with only a spinner
fixes.problem: Model calls, retries and self-checks took real time with nothing on screen.
fixes.fix: The loop streams status events with a title and reason, and every model call, tool call and worker is timed into a Case file waterfall and a live process graph.
fixes.result: The user can see what is happening and where the time goes.

releases.servicesTitle: Part 2 · The AI services we use, and why
releases.servicesIntro: Agent One uses several kinds of AI service, each for a different job. The rule throughout is: use the cheapest service that does the job well, always have a free fallback, and never advertise a service that is not configured.

services.title: Language models (the agent's brain)
rows: Main model: designs agents, runs the agent loop, workers, briefs and judges.
Fast (3-5 s a call), runs from the droplet, cheap on the paid plan ($0.011 per 1,000 neurons past the free allowance).
Free fallback and local development on the RTX 2070 SUPER.
No cost and no quota. Slower, one request at a time, so it is the last resort. Not on the droplet.
Optional first choice when it has credits; also image generation and embeddings.
Strong and fast, but prepaid credits ran out, so the app skips it on 402 and does not depend on it.

services.title: Embeddings (meaning as numbers)
rows: Finds similar past agents to use as examples when building a new one (retrieval-augmented generation), and spots duplicate or related Focus topics in Setup.
Grounds the design in agents that worked before instead of starting cold. Fails quietly to “no grounding”.

services.title: Tool servers over MCP (the agent's hands)
rows: Current time and time zones; reading a web page.
Vetted, free and reliable, so the model does not write its own versions.
Good results, built for agents; limited monthly credits.
Fallback web search when Tavily is at its limit.
Free with no card; keeps search working all month.
Publishes a chosen agent as a tool other apps (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, jobfit) can call.
Makes Agent One a building block, not only a website.

services.title: Images
rows: Creates images an agent is asked for.
Hugging Face is free, so images still work without Gemini credits.
Finds real photos for a topic.
Wikipedia is free and always available.

services.title: Quality control (AI checking AI)
rows: Grades each bootstrap, reply, tool call and worker.
Catches weak answers and gives every model a track record.
Screens replies against the out-of-scope list.
A judge with no tools or persona is much harder to talk round.
Recommends a model from that track record, while still trying new ones.
Model choice based on data, not guesses. Advisory only.
Runs fixed cases against each model with recorded tool replies.

releases.closing: Agent One now runs on a fast, low-cost hosted model with a free local fallback, two web search providers that cover for each other, generated tools that are checked before they run and sandboxed when they do, and a record of every step the agent takes. Remaining known limits are listed in `CLAUDE.md`: per-user accounts, server-side chat history, durable file output, and a stricter sandbox (separate user or container, network allowlist).
